candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor with an Ed.D. in Community Care and Counseling: Traumatology and more than 15 years of experience in behavioral health, clinical services, and program leadership, I bring a strong commitment to providing high-quality, trauma-informed care to adolescents and families.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with youth experiencing complex behavioral health challenges, trauma histories, family instability, and barriers to accessing appropriate treatment. In my leadership role with Partners Health Management, I have overseen behavioral health initiatives across a 15-county service area, supervised multidisciplinary teams, and helped develop and implement specialized programs designed to improve access to services, strengthen care coordination, and reduce unnecessary higher levels of care.  One of my greatest professional strengths is combining clinical expertise with operational leadership. I have experience supporting clinical decision-making, establishing effective workflows, monitoring quality and compliance, mentoring staff, and collaborating with families, community providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies. I understand the importance of developing a clinical environment where staff feel supported, families feel heard, and adolescents receive individualized, evidence-based treatment.

My doctoral research focused on the experiences of social workers placing youth in residential treatment within North Carolina's child welfare system. This work further strengthened my understanding of the challenges adolescents and families face when appropriate community-based behavioral health services are unavailable. I am particularly passionate about developing programs that intervene earlier, promote stability, and help youth receive effective treatment in the least restrictive appropriate setting.

The opportunity to contribute to the development and leadership of Adolescent Wellness Academy's North Carolina program is especially appealing. I would welcome the opportunity to help establish a strong clinical culture, support staff development, build community partnerships, and ensure that adolescents and families receive compassionate, effective, and accountable care.  Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to adolescent mental health could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's success.

Sincerely,
April L. Rorabaugh, Ed.D., LCMHC

I would love the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and dedication to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you about how I can contribute to your team.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

Your remote position for the Bilingual Virtual Intake Coordinator sounds like an amazing opportunity. I would love to join the team and begin to make a difference in this field. I think I would be a great fit for this role for a few specific reasons.

For nearly five years, I was housed by the state of Washington in a middle school as a Student Assistant Professional. It was a title that wouldn’t scare students away, not as scary sounding as a “drug and alcohol counselor”. In this role I did both prevention and intervention work with students impacted by substance use, either their own or a loved one in their lives. I worked with teachers and students, and built partnerships with parents and community organizations. When a student needed services, I would introduce myself, conduct an intake form including a few different mental health screening tools, contact parents, place them in a group or individual sessions, and track their progress over time. I worked with both English and Spanish speaking families. I was extremely passionate about this work and loved my students dearly. The skills and empathy I learned from this job were life changing and could be such a good fit for this role as the intake coordinator. 

My teenage and young adult years I worked in a variety of customer service roles. I can work well to de-escalate situations and work hard to get people the best support they need, for whatever they are looking for. I have a strong sense of empathy and can convey this in person, over the phone, and through writing. I am organized, a team player, and motivated to complete the tasks set before me. I am efficient using Microsoft, Google suite, and have a typing speed of 65 WPM. I am quick to learn any new computer based program and can thrive in a remote based position. 

Most recently, I have worked the last four years as a substitute teacher and a high school teacher. I truly find joy working with teenagers, which is another reason this is a great fit!

I would love to connect  and provide any additional details about my experience and abilities. I can confidently and humbly say that I have made better any organization I have worked for and served. I am looking forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely, 
Alissa Seda Shaw

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my bilingual communication skills, organizational ability, and genuine commitment to adolescent well-being to your team. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Intake Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy.  I am passionate about mental health and particularly enjoy working with adolescents. I believe that every young person has a unique way of understanding the world, and one of the things I value most about working with them is that I learn so much from each individual and their thought process. I find it meaningful to understand their perspectives, recognize their needs, and contribute to an environment where they feel heard, respected, and supported; it matter to me the most to provide a safe space for each and everyone of them.

Through my psychology practicums, I have gained experience conducting psychological assessments with adolescents, administering and interpreting psychological tests, and participating in interventions focused on adolescent development, family unity, and violence prevention. I have also worked with children who have experienced abandonment or violence, which has strengthened my empathy and taught me the importance of approaching sensitive situations with patience, care, and professionalism.

I consider myself a highly empathetic, adaptable, and resourceful person. I learn quickly, think critically, and enjoy finding practical solutions when challenges arise. I understand that supporting adolescents and their families involves not only compassion but also organization, clear communication, and attention to detail. I am comfortable working with Zoom and digital tools, and I would be confident managing virtual interactions while helping families navigate the intake process and ensuring that information is communicated accurately to the appropriate team members.

As a native Spanish speaker with C1-level English proficiency, I can communicate effectively with families in both languages and help create a more accessible and welcoming experience. I would be excited to contribute my psychological background, interpersonal skills, and genuine interest in adolescent well-being to AWA's mission of supporting young people and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, motivation, and skills could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Mariana Ochoa Ortiz

education.summary: I am currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Psychology at Universidad Iberoamericana in Mexico City. My academic training has provided me with a strong foundation in psychological assessment, human development, mental health, and individual and group interventions. Through coursework and practical experiences, I have developed critical thinking, empathy, and communication skills, with a particular interest in adolescent development and emotional well-being. I am eager to apply my knowledge to support individuals and families while continuing to grow professionally.

I completed a semester abroad at Concordia University in Montreal, Canada, from January to May 2026, as part of my Psychology degree at Universidad Iberoamericana. This experience strengthened my adaptability, independence, cross-cultural communication, and ability to navigate new environments. Studying in an international setting also allowed me to develop greater confidence communicating in English and collaborating with people from diverse backgrounds.

Hiring Committee

Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Admissions and Intake position. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology, one year of experience as a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT), and two years as a Behavior Coach, I have developed a strong foundation in understanding mental health challenges, supporting individuals and families, and approaching each interaction with compassion and empathy.

My experience has reinforced the importance of meeting individuals where they are emotionally and helping them navigate difficult situations with patience, understanding, and respect. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be overwhelming, and I am committed to ensuring that every caller feels heard, supported, and guided toward an appropriate next step.

I bring experience with intake and admissions responsibilities, inbound calls and referrals, scheduling assessments and appointments, maintaining HIPAA-compliant records, and following up with clients and families. My background in behavioral health has strengthened my communication, organization, and ability to build rapport with individuals facing challenging circumstances. Additionally, my experience working in both remote and onsite settings has helped me adapt to different work environments while remaining focused on providing consistent, dependable support.

What draws me to this opportunity is the chance to combine my psychology education and hands-on behavioral health experience to help individuals access the care they need. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your admissions team through compassionate communication, attention to detail, and a genuine commitment to supporting individuals and families throughout the intake process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background, empathy, and dedication to mental health can contribute to your team and help individuals take the first step toward recovery and well-being.

Sincerely,
Skylar

Dear Wellness Academy
I am writing to express my heartfelt interest in the Adolescent Intake Specialist position. Through my work in mental health, I have learned that the intake process is much more than an administrative step—it is often the very first moment a struggling teenager and their family feel seen, heard, and safe. I am deeply drawn to dedication to youth and adult wellness, and I would love to bring my gentle approach, crisis screening experience, and commitment to trauma-informed care to your team.
In my previous role at Cognitive behavioral center, I guided adolescents/adults and their guardians through initial assessments during some of the most overwhelming moments of their lives. I understand that teenagers facing mental health or behavioral challenges often present with walls built high out of fear or pain. By leading with patience, active listening, and a non-judgmental presence, I have been able to help vulnerable youth lower their defenses, allowing for accurate risk assessments regarding safety, substance use, and emotional distress.
Equally important to my clinical screening skills is my ability to support families. I make it a priority to anchor worried parents, explaining next steps clearly to ease their anxiety while strictly upholding HIPAA privacy rules and minor consent standards. I am highly skilled at collaborating closely with therapists, doctors, and school advocates to ensure that every teenager's transition into care is seamless, dignified, and rooted in a sense of hope.
I would be honored to bring my dedication to youth advocacy and my calm, grounding energy to your intake department. Thank you for your time, consideration, and the vital work you do for our community's youth. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my experience can support your families.
With care and respect,
-Alicia

October 19, 2026
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Agency:
I heard about this job opportunity through Indeed and thought it would be a great fit. I have experience working in a drug & alcohol rehab center as the administrative assistant. We worked with adults and youth. I’m excited for this opportunity as my past work experience and degree make me a perfect candidate for this role.

In my previous role as administrative assistant at Managed Care Center, I worked with youth daily and helped to make a true difference in their lives. They would come to us usually because they were required rather than wanting to get help. We were the first people they would come in contact with. Many were upset, lost, and a little broken, and it was our job to help them in this life changing journey. To make things a little easier for them and for them to understand that they had support. I am a very patient and compassionate person. I hold myself to a higher standard. My goal not only in my work but in life is to truly make a difference in people's lives. 

I’m inspired by this company and the mission to help youth in their most trying moments. I want to do my part in aiding those in need and helping them in their journey to recovery and a healthier & happier life. This cause is very near to my heart as I have a teenager who has struggled with mental health & addiction issues. 

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills align with Adolescent Wellness Academy's goals in an interview. 


With best regards,
Jessica Garcia

questionnaire.response: I successfully completed this clinical graduate internship upon graduating with my Master of Arts in Forensic Mental Health Counseling. questionnaire.text: If we asked this supervisor about your performance, what would they say was your most significant area for growth, and why?
questionnaire.response: My supervisor would say that I tend to take on too much personal responsibility before asking for backup. During my clinical intake internship, I wanted to make sure our patient registries and data entry were completely flawless, so I would spend a lot of time independently fixing errors myself. My supervisor coached me on the fact that while being independent and protective of data integrity is a strength—especially for remote roles—it is more efficient to pull in teammates early when troubleshooting complex pipelines. I learned to communicate my progress sooner, allowing me to maintain high accuracy while keeping the office workflow moving quickly.

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an organization that helps individuals and families navigate mental health and substance use treatment with compassion, understanding, and support.
I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an emotional and challenging experience for individuals and their loved ones. I believe that providing a welcoming, patient, and professional first point of contact can make a meaningful difference in someone's journey toward recovery. I would approach every call and inquiry with empathy, respect, and a commitment to helping each person understand their options and take the next step toward receiving care.
I would bring a strong commitment to communication, organization, confidentiality, and follow-through to this role. I understand the importance of responding to inquiries promptly, coordinating appointments and assessments, maintaining accurate records, and ensuring that each caller receives appropriate guidance. I am also prepared to learn and work within the systems and procedures necessary to support efficient admissions coordination while protecting sensitive client information.
What interests me most about this opportunity is the chance to combine administrative responsibilities with meaningful work that positively impacts people's lives. I would welcome the opportunity to support your admissions team by helping clients and families feel heard, respected, and supported throughout the intake process.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my skills, dedication, and compassionate approach could contribute to your team. I look forward to the possibility of joining your organization and supporting individuals and families as they take important steps toward healing and recovery.
Sincerely,
Yahni Goodwyn

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my direct experience in crisis intervention, behavioral health support, and remote administrative operations, I am confident I can meet callers with the compassion and competence your team requires during their most vulnerable moments.

My background uniquely positions me for this role. As a Crisis Intervention Specialist at the Family Violence Prevention Center, I answered a 24-hour crisis hotline, screening individuals for intake and providing critical support during acute crises. I understand firsthand how to engage someone on one of the hardest days of their lives—listening with empathy, asking the right questions, and guiding them toward clear next steps. I also coordinated legal interventions, referrals, and services across multiple stakeholders, experience that translates directly to connecting families with appropriate treatment options and ensuring consistent follow-up.

My time as a Community Reentry Specialist at Alvis 180 Degree Impact deepened my knowledge of behavioral health and substance use treatment. I conducted biopsychosocial assessments, formulated individualized service plans, and utilized motivational engagement techniques—all skills essential for screening clients for PHP and IOP programs in plain, caring language. I'm experienced in working within multidisciplinary clinical environments and maintaining accurate, compliant client records.

Since 2022, I've successfully managed remote work responsibilities at Speedway/7-Eleven as a Data Analyst, where I developed strong self-management skills, maintained workflow calendars, and resolved 30+ cases monthly by taking initiative without daily direction. I'm proficient in CRM and EMR systems, having organized and maintained patient data while ensuring HIPAA compliance at the Family Violence Prevention Center. I also excel at data validation, accuracy, and tracking—skills that will ensure every lead is properly documented and no caller falls through the cracks.

What sets me apart is my genuine commitment to service. Throughout my career, I've prioritized building rapport with vulnerable populations, communicating with clarity and warmth, and following through on commitments. My combination of crisis intervention expertise, treatment knowledge, remote work experience, and technical proficiency makes me an excellent fit for this role.

I look forward to discussing your needs and my background and qualifications in greater detail.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Felicia Wilson

October 19, 2026

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization in a position focused on adolescent mental health and substance abuse treatment. With a strong educational foundation in clinical psychology, professional experience in substance abuse counseling, and a passion for supporting children and adolescents experiencing emotional and behavioral challenges, I believe my background would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

I earned my Bachelor of Science in Clinical Psychology with a minor in Human Development and Family Studies from Anderson University. I am currently pursuing my Master of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Liberty University, where I continue to expand my knowledge of counseling theories, clinical assessment, evidence-based interventions, and treatment approaches for individuals experiencing mental health and substance use disorders.

My professional experience includes working as an Alcohol and Drug Counselor at Palmetto Carolina Treatment Center, where I provided counseling and support to individuals experiencing substance use disorders. In this role, I gained valuable experience in treatment planning, clinical documentation, client education, and supporting individuals throughout their recovery journeys. Additionally, my previous experience as an Early Interventionist with Easterseals allowed me to work closely with children and families to address developmental, emotional, and behavioral needs.

In my current position as a Classroom Therapeutic Provider, I work directly with children experiencing behavioral and emotional challenges. My responsibilities include implementing individualized therapeutic interventions, promoting emotional regulation, teaching healthy coping strategies, maintaining progress documentation, and collaborating with other professionals to support treatment goals. These experiences have strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, respond effectively to challenging behaviors, and provide compassionate, individualized support.

I am particularly passionate about working with adolescents who are navigating mental health concerns, substance use challenges, and difficult life circumstances. I recognize the importance of early intervention, positive therapeutic relationships, and providing young individuals with the tools necessary to make healthier decisions and achieve long-term stability.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and developing clinical knowledge to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to further discuss how my qualifications align with the needs of your team.

Sincerely,
Jessica Hallums

​Sincerely,
​Saray Lira

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my background working with children, adolescents, and adults facing mental health challenges, substance use concerns, and behavioral difficulties, I believe I can bring compassion, patience, and a genuine desire to help others to your team.

One of the most rewarding aspects of my work is seeing someone reach a goal they once thought was difficult or out of reach. Knowing that I played even a small part in helping someone feel proud, confident, and hopeful is what motivates me to continue doing this work. I understand that reaching out for support can be overwhelming for individuals and their families, and I would approach every admissions interaction with empathy, professionalism, and a commitment to making people feel heard and supported.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, dedication, and passion for helping others could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of joining your team and making a meaningful difference in the lives of the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Ashley Litteer

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. As a recent graduate with a bachelor’s degree in Psychology and a minor in Social Work, I am passionate about helping adolescents and families access the support and resources they need.

Through my experience in customer service, retail management, and working with children as a camp counselor, I have developed strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills. I understand the importance of being patient, compassionate, and professional when working with individuals and families who may be going through difficult situations. I am comfortable communicating with others, answering questions, and helping people feel supported.

I am especially interested in this position because I want to build a career in mental health and substance use treatment, particularly working with adolescents. I would welcome the opportunity to use my education and interpersonal skills to help families navigate the admissions process and connect them with the appropriate care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and passion for helping others would make me a strong candidate for this position.

Sincerely,
Paige Richards

I also bring previous remote work experience, which has equipped me with the discipline, organizational skills, accountability, and ability to communicate effectively in a virtual environment. Combined with my healthcare customer service background, I am confident in my ability to manage responsibilities independently while maintaining professionalism, accuracy, and a high standard of service.
What draws me most to Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to combine my professional experience with my genuine passion for helping young people and families navigate difficult circumstances. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in remote customer service, direct support services, client documentation, and administrative operations, I bring a combination of communication, organization, confidentiality, and client-centered support skills that align with the needs of your admissions team.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed the ability to manage high-volume interactions, gather and verify information, maintain accurate electronic records, and communicate with clients professionally and compassionately. In my remote customer service role with Royal Asset Management, I managed more than 100 client interactions daily while updating records, researching concerns, and providing timely follow-up. My experience with ConServe has further strengthened my ability to document interactions, handle sensitive information, and navigate client concerns while maintaining compliance and accuracy.

My experience as a Direct Support Professional with All Caring Hands also gave me valuable exposure to individualized support, client well-being, care documentation, and communication with families and team members. I understand the importance of treating people with dignity, recognizing individual needs, and handling sensitive situations with patience and professionalism. I would bring that same thoughtful approach to supporting individuals and families as they explore behavioral health and substance use treatment options.

Beyond my professional background, I am the creator of Grounded & Growing with Syi, a personal blog that explores mental health, motherhood, faith, and personal growth. Through this platform, I encourage open conversations about emotional well-being and navigating life’s challenges. My interest in mental health advocacy is one of the reasons this opportunity is especially meaningful to me. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be a vulnerable first step, and I would strive to make every caller feel respected, heard, and supported while helping them understand the next steps in the admissions process.

I am also comfortable working in remote environments, using CRM systems, maintaining electronic records, and managing multiple responsibilities while meeting accuracy and productivity expectations. I understand the importance of confidentiality and careful documentation when handling sensitive client information. I am eager to apply these transferable skills while learning your organization’s admissions procedures, insurance verification processes, and electronic medical record systems.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, reliability, and passion for helping others to your team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and commitment to compassionate client support could benefit Adolescent Wellness Academy or Principles Recovery Center.

Dear Hiring Team at Principles Recovery Center,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center. My background in behavioral health admissions and care coordination has centered on exactly what this role requires: managing high-volume inquiries, screening prospective clients, coordinating admissions, navigating insurance and financial barriers, and keeping clients and families engaged throughout the admissions process.

In my previous behavioral health roles, I have managed the admissions process from initial inquiry through placement, including client screening and qualification, insurance verification, prior authorizations, financial coordination, intake scheduling, referral management, and ongoing follow-up. I am also experienced with Kipu and EMR documentation, HIPAA compliance, and working closely with clinical teams, providers, families, and referral partners to ensure clients move into the appropriate level of care efficiently. 

What particularly interests me about Principles Recovery Center is the opportunity to combine strong admissions operations with the personal side of the work. In substance use treatment, a prospective client or family member may be reaching out during an incredibly vulnerable moment. I understand the importance of building trust quickly, communicating treatment options clearly, maintaining consistent follow-up, and removing barriers that could prevent someone from entering care.

I am comfortable independently managing a fast-moving admissions pipeline while maintaining accurate documentation and consistent communication. My experience has taught me how to balance compassion with urgency—keeping prospective clients engaged while coordinating the clinical, financial, and logistical pieces necessary to move an admission forward.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioral health admissions experience, knowledge of the treatment process, and commitment to strong client follow-through to Principles Recovery Center. Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to your admissions team and the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Emily Allieri

Dear Hiring Manager,

With a strong background in healthcare enrollment, patient communication, and remote customer service, I bring the organization, attention to detail, and compassion needed to help individuals and families navigate important healthcare decisions.

I would approach every interaction with empathy, respect, and a commitment to helping callers understand their options and take the next steps toward care. I am comfortable working independently in a remote environment, using technology to manage information, and following through to ensure tasks are completed accurately and efficiently.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, strong communication skills, and dedication to helping others to your admissions team. I am especially interested in contributing to an organization that helps individuals and families access the care and support they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Janelle Brock

Dear Hiring Team,

When someone calls about treatment for themselves or their teen, they are often scared, tired, and unsure what to ask. I want to be the calm, caring voice that helps them take the next step. I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role, and I would be glad to support either Adolescent Wellness Academy or Principles Recovery Center.

As a Certified Clinical Medical Assistant in family medicine and urgent care, I was often the first person patients spoke with. I checked patients in, gathered their history, confirmed insurance details, and entered information in the EMR while keeping it private under HIPAA. Urgent care taught me to stay steady when people arrive upset, in pain, or afraid. I learned to listen first, explain next steps in plain words, and make sure no one left without knowing what came next.

I am used to managing my own work without daily direction. Running Beyond Scrubs while studying and working means I set my own schedule, track my own tasks, and follow through on every open item. I keep a clear record of each contact and follow up until every person has a next step. I learn new systems quickly, from EMRs to the online tools I use to run my business, and I would bring that same habit to your CRM and to Kipu.

Your programs give teens, adults, and families a real path to healing. I would be proud to be the first voice they hear on that path. Thank you for your time. I look forward to talking with you about how I can support your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Anary Bellamy, CCMA

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my excitement and sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. Having worked directly within behavioral health intake, client screening, and insurance verification, I understand the technical precision and care required to guide individuals into that next step that they don't even know yet they deserve. Beyond my clinical and operational experience, this work is deeply personal to me.

I understand how important that first phone call is, and how scary it is, because I still remember mine. I remember the person on the other end of the phone, who made me feel safe, not judged, and reassured me that I was strong enough to walk through the hard decisions, and that I deserved this for myself. The kindness and assurance of that single call changed my life, and it is the exact environment of safety, respect, and dignity I aim to create for every caller reaching out for help.

For the past five years, I have served as a leader with Celebrate Recovery, including serving as the female leader for The Landing—a youth ministry branch where I mentored teenage girls through mental health challenges, addiction, and difficult life struggles. Combining this hands-on community leadership with my professional background in behavioral health, intake assessments and HIPAA compliance allows me to meet callers in their most vulnerable moments with absolute empathy, operational discipline, and a commitment that no patient gets lost in the process.

I would be honored for the opportunity to discuss how my background and personal dedication align with your admissions team. 

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Misty Lilly

With my diverse experience as a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT), Psychiatric Technician, and Administrative Assistant in funeral service, as well as an Apprentice Funeral Director, I am confident in becoming an asset to your team. My career experience has provided me with compassionate communication, independent decision making skills, and HIPAA-compliant documentation. My background has also equipped me to answer inbound inquiries of a sensitive nature, screening and triaging calls, verifying insurance, scheduling meetings and providing assessments, while ensuring a seamless experience for clients, families, and providers. Whether working unsupervised in critical and emotional environments or collaborating with management teams, I always prioritize clarity, empathy, and efficiency in my daily work.

In my current role as a Psychiatric Technician, I operate independently and unsupervised, managing patient care, documenting progress, and facilitating therapeutic activities with care and thoughtfulness. As an RBT, I communicated regularly with caregivers, providing updates on therapy progress and adjusting treatment plans collaboratively. My experience in funeral service administration and directing, further honed my ability to handle sensitive inquiries with care, manage complex scheduling, and maintain meticulous records; skills that directly translate to this role. I am adept at explaining complex processes in clear, empathetic language and ensure every detail and concern is addressed with professionalism.

I am confident in my ability to track leads in CRM and EMR systems, having prior experience with clinical data collection, scheduling, billing and progress tracking. I am confident in following up consistently, ensuring every caller is scheduled or appropriately referred. My combination of clinical, administrative, and behavioral health experience allows me to approach this role with both compassion and organizational expertise, ensuring a smooth and supportive admissions process. I am excited at the opportunity to contribute to your team and am available at your convenience for an interview if you choose to consider me for this role.

Sincerely,

Laura Lopez

Hi,
I am writing to express my interest in the advertised position. With over a decade of combined experience in clinical mental health, organizational psychology, and higher education, I bring a unique balance of therapeutic insight, leadership acumen, and evidence-based practice to support both individual and systemic transformation.

I am deeply motivated by opportunities that allow me to merge my clinical grounding, academic leadership, and consulting expertise to advance holistic mental health, organizational wellness, and educational excellence. I am confident that my blend of compassion, analytical rigor, and collaborative leadership would contribute significantly to your team’s goals and mission.

Thank you for your consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and values align with your organization’s priorities. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your continued success.

Rosilyn Sanders

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With my experience in care coordination, admissions, telehealth, and behavioral health, along with my current work as a Certified Peer Specialist and my ongoing pursuit of a Bachelor of Science in Human Services at Columbia Southern University, I believe I would be a strong addition to your team.

Through my care coordination experience, I have developed skills in admissions, client communication, telehealth services, and helping individuals navigate the process of accessing care. My background in behavioral health has strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, coordinate services, maintain accurate documentation, and provide compassionate support to individuals experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, organization, confidentiality, and helping individuals understand their options so they can take the next step toward treatment.

In my role as a Certified Peer Specialist, I continue to build meaningful connections with individuals by meeting them with empathy, respect, and an understanding of the challenges that can accompany recovery. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be overwhelming for individuals and their families. I would bring a patient, reassuring, and professional approach to every interaction while helping callers feel heard and supported throughout the admissions process.

I am comfortable communicating by phone and through telehealth, managing responsibilities independently, coordinating follow-up, and documenting services accurately. I also understand the importance of protecting confidential information and maintaining professionalism when handling sensitive client information. I am confident that my combination of care coordination, admissions, and direct behavioral health experience would allow me to contribute positively to your team.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my administrative and coordination skills with my passion for helping people access the behavioral health services they need. I would welcome the opportunity to support your admissions team and help individuals and families navigate the path toward treatment and recovery.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and commitment to behavioral health could benefit your organization.

Sincerely,
Allisha Hamilton

NICOLE BELL, BA
HEALTHCARE COORDINATION • PATIENT ADVOCACY • BEHAVIORAL HEALTH
North Miami Beach, FL | bell0081.n@gmail.com | www.linkedin.com/in/bell0081

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am a Psychology graduate with professional experience in healthcare coordination, patient access, health compliance, medical records, and clinical operations. In my current role at Florida International University, I support clinical operations and patient services within a university health center while independently managing a substantial health-compliance workload that requires accuracy, judgment, communication, and follow-through. My work goes beyond checking people in and managing appointments. I regularly review electronically
submitted health documentation to determine whether it meets university and applicable state requirements, identify missing or incomplete information, enter qualifying immunizations, upload records, and remove health-compliance holds when requirements are satisfied. When something does not meet the requirements, I communicate directly with the student, explain what is missing or incorrect, and help them determine where they may be able to obtain the documentation they need. A significant part of my role is problem-solving. When a student does not know where to find a vaccination record or other required documentation, I work through the situation with them and identify practical options
based on their circumstances. I have learned that resolving these issues effectively requires more than simply knowing the requirements. It requires listening carefully, identifying the actual barrier, explaining the
answer clearly, and making sure the person understands what needs to happen next.
I also independently coordinate the patient experience from check-in through checkout. This includes verifying forms and eligibility, supporting nurse and provider workflow, scheduling appointments, answering questions, explaining charges, processing payments, and directing patients to the appropriate department when an issue falls outside my area. I also complete daily payment reporting across multiple systems and prepare the supporting documentation required for Accounting. The volume of my compliance work has given me experience working accurately under pressure. During
the summer 2026 enrollment period, I handled a high volume of inbound calls and electronically submitted immunization and waiver documentation while continuing to manage clinical operations and patient services. My Psychology degree has strengthened my understanding of human behavior, development, adjustment,
psychopathology, psychotherapy, and health and illness. My professional experience has taught me how to apply that understanding in real interactions with people who may be confused, frustrated, overwhelmed, or
simply unsure of what to do next. I value being able to make complicated processes easier for people to understand while still maintaining accuracy and the requirements of the organization. I am now looking to bring this combination of psychology, healthcare experience, patient advocacy, service navigation, documentation, problem-solving, and independent workflow management into a remote healthcare coordination, patient navigation, patient advocacy, or behavioral-health support position. Thank you for your consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Nicole Bell

work_history.title: Recruiting Manager
work_history.summary: (Remote position) I am currently the recruiting manager for this oilfield company. They are a third party contractor and work for all of the southern United States. I hire employees (using indeed) as they need more people for their crews. I handle all applications, interviews, onboarding paperwork and safety training for each employee.

work_history.title: Dental Assistant/Treatment Coordinator
work_history.summary: I worked for Dr. Haynie in Coushatta and she bought this practice in May 2018. I was brought in as an assistant in December 2018 and later also gained the title of treatment coordinator. Duties: Chart audit for the day, make sure all lab cases are on track for pickup/ delivery to and from our office and make sure the patient has a scheduled appointment, set up my operatory for each procedure, follow all safety and sterilization protocols, take inventory and order all needed materials monthly, put away any order deliveries once I verify all contents in the delivery, take x-rays/impressions/ pre and post op procedure photos. I also use a Great Lakes mini star to create Essex retainers/ bleach trays, and occasionally a bruxism splint. Crowns/Onlays Scan crown/onlay preps using omni cam, design crown and start the milling process, once crown is made I try it into place on the tooth and verify margins and contacts, once I verify that crown/onlay fits how it should then I stain/ glaze it and place in the oven to finish processing. Once crown/onlay is finished in the oven, I etch and silinate the restoration and get the patient ready for Dr. Haynie to bond it. Once restoration is cemented, excess cement is cleaned up, and occlusion is adjusted, I take a bitewing x-ray to verify the margins and that there is no excess cement interproximally. On certain occasions we decide to place a temporary restoration and in that case I am the one that creates those, adjusts contacts/ margins/occlusion and cement with temporary cement. Dr. Haynie comes in to verify once I am finished. I then go over post op instructions and get the patient set up for their next appointment and get any prescriptions if they are needed. Treatment Coordinator: I see all new patients to do paperwork and get them comfortable to speak with Dr. Haynie. Normally once the patient gets seated in the operatory we have a basic conversation about who they are, what their dental goals are, their family, and what they do for a living just to calm their nerves and get them to feel comfortable talking to us. Once we get comfortable with each other I take a full mouth x-ray series, intraoral/extra oral photos, and depending on the case I even take study models. Once Dr. Haynie does her exam, I chart all existing treatment and treatment that she recommended. Before the patient leaves I give them treatment plans and thoroughly go over it with them explaining the treatment verbally and with videos/models. Once patient understands, we then get them scheduled or give them 2 weeks to think about it and then I reach out by phone call to see if they have any further questions or if they would like to go ahead and schedule. When our receptionist is out of the office I take over her responsibilities by checking phone messages and our texting system (solution reach), verify insurance, check patients in and out of the office, file insurance claims and take payments in person/over the phone/ and by mail. Process end of day and make sure all collections match up at the end of the day. I also send x-rays/notes, referrals to the specialists that we refer to.

work_history.title: Orthodontic Assistant/receptionist
work_history.summary: Bonded braces (placed cheek retractor and NOLA, pumiced teeth, rinsed, dried, etched, rinsed, dried, painted on assure plus, dried, placed brackets, Call Dr to check placement of brackets, light cured brackets, placed wires, cut wires to length or would cinch the wires, placed stops on wires), removed braces, replaced broken/loose brackets, took panoramic and ceph xrays, took impressions, bonded permanent retainers, instructed each patient how to brush and floss and take care of their braces, changed out archwires, placed power chains/colors, delivered pushdown and Hawley retainers. Experienced in digital intraoral scanning for invisalign. Also all of the girls rotated as receptionist on Fridays. *used dolphin computer program*

work_history.title: Dental Assistant/Receptionist
work_history.summary: I get to work early to set up my operatories, set up trays for the day, make sure all rooms and tools are sterile, I work chairside with the Drs., I take x-rays and impressions and then pour the impression up into a stone 3-D form, I keep track of all things that need to be ordered, I keep everything organized and all of the operatories stocked with things needed daily, I refill burr blocks, refill water containers (for our drills), I run the suction lines with a special cleaner, I change our traps for our suctions, sterilize rooms and all of the tools, perform monthly and weekly maintenance on autoclave, currently helping train the new front desk receptionist, and I help the dentist in any way I possibly can.

work_history.title: Dental Assistant/Receptionist
work_history.summary: Every morning I would get to work early, sign in, turn on the lights and computers, check the voicemail for messages, then I would go to my operatory and look on my computer for the patients I would be working on, I would write down their important info such as procedure and allergies and set up tray for the dr to use, I would assist the dr in all procedures. My duties included (suctioning, retracting the tongue and cheek, flinging out tooth color for composite for the fillings, assist in root canals, crowns, sealants, I would take each patients X-rays, load syringe for the dr to inject patient, get the right extraction tools, filling tools and material and everything else the dr needed, once each procedure was done I would disinfect room and tools that were used, print up tx plans and prescription and prepare for next patient) I continued to work for a few more months even after quitting at Hudds but later had to quit here as well due to my high risk pregnancy.

work_history.title: Waitress/Cashier
work_history.summary: Each day I got to work I would make the tea and coffee, serve customers their food and drinks, clean the tables, wash dishes, take to go orders on the phone, and also work the register for my customers. It was a small restaurant so each waitress had about 5-10 tables at once, and was responsible for working the register for their customers and taking turns taking the to go orders on the phone. It was almost always really busy. Then at the end of the night I would sweep, finish up the dishes, wipe all the tables down and then leave. I worked there and at amazing smiles during the same time. I had to quit job due to high risk pregnancy. (Also served alcohol to legal customers)

**Jasmine Curry**  
Brooklyn, NY  
929-435-9996  
jcurryt@gmail.com  

October 19, 2026 

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy or Principles Recovery Center. With over 10 years of experience in client engagement, case management, customer service, and program coordination, I have developed a strong foundation in conducting assessments, identifying individual needs, coordinating referrals, and providing compassionate support to individuals navigating challenging circumstances. I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to apply my experience in client-centered services to help individuals and families connect with appropriate treatment and support.

In my current role as an Employment Coach with Equus Workforce | WeCARE, I manage a high volume caseload of approximately 150–200 clients, conducting intake interviews, vocational assessments, and ongoing evaluations to identify individual needs and develop individualized service plans. The individuals I serve experience a wide range of medical barriers, including physical and mental health challenges, substance use concerns, and social and economic hardships that can affect their stability and access to services. My experience includes working with individuals experiencing homelessness, veterans, and justice impacted clients, as well as assisting clients with substance use issues who require referrals to CASAC services and outpatient treatment programs. Through individualized case management, I help clients identify appropriate resources, navigate barriers to care, and connect with services that support their well-being and long-term stability.

I also conduct weekly virtual and in-person follow ups to monitor client progress, assess ongoing needs, and provide continued support. During the COVID-19 pandemic, I worked remotely while conducting wellness follow ups and connecting clients with appropriate resources. Managing a caseload of this size has strengthened my ability to prioritize competing responsibilities, maintain organized records, communicate effectively, and ensure consistent engagement with clients and service providers.

Additionally, I utilize HIPAA compliant systems for ongoing case management, evaluations, and documentation, understanding the importance of confidentiality and accuracy when handling sensitive client information. My experience with intake assessments, progress tracking, outreach, and treatment referrals provides a strong foundation for managing admissions inquiries, coordinating assessments and intake paperwork, communicating with referral partners, and maintaining accurate client records throughout the admissions process.

My previous leadership experience with American Airlines and Turkish Airlines further strengthened my customer service, problem-solving, and communication skills. I regularly addressed escalated concerns, de-escalated challenging interactions, coordinated with multiple departments, and maintained accuracy in fast-paced environments. These experiences have prepared me to communicate confidently with clients, families, and referral partners while approaching sensitive conversations with patience, empathy, and professionalism.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my remote work experience, assessment skills, high-volume caseload management, treatment referral coordination, and commitment to client-centered service to your admissions team. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be a vulnerable and important step for individuals and families. I would strive to make each caller feel heard and respected while providing clear information, timely follow up, and support in navigating the next steps toward appropriate care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my background in case management, substance use treatment referrals, client advocacy, and service coordination could contribute to your team's mission of helping individuals and families access the care they need.

Best Regards,  
- Jasmine Curry

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

Thank you for reaching out about the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role. The first call about treatment often decides whether someone ever walks through the door, and I would welcome the chance to be the first voice families and adults hear when they call Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.
For three years, through April 2024, I worked as a Substance Use Disorder Professional (SUDP) in the withdrawal management unit at Lifeline Connections in Vancouver, Washington. That work maps closely to what your coordinators do:

• Screening for fit: I completed ASAM assessments and medical necessity screenings to determine the right level of care, and served on the admissions clinical review team that approved or denied placements. I know how to tell whether PHP, IOP, or another setting is the right next step, and how to explain it in plain, caring language.

• Insurance: I handled commercial insurance pre-authorizations, so verifying benefits and securing approval before an intake date is familiar work.

• Follow-through and referrals: When we weren't the right fit, I referred people to other agencies and coordinated with outside providers to make transitions seamless, so no one left without a clear next step.

• Accurate, HIPAA-compliant records: Electronic health record documentation was part of every shift, held to Washington DOH standards for assessment, placement, and referral.

Families are often the ones making that first call, especially for teens. Communicating with families was a regular part of my patient management at Lifeline, and before that at Sharon Care Center and as a Certified Nursing Assistant and Medication Aide. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in social services, crisis intervention, substance use recovery support, virtual client assessments, and case management, I have developed a strong commitment to helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances and connect with the care and resources they need. I am excited about the opportunity to bring my compassion, communication skills, and organizational strengths to your team while helping individuals take the first steps toward recovery and improved mental health.

In my most recent role as a Police Assisted Social Worker with the Goose Creek Police Department, I responded to overdose incidents alongside law enforcement personnel, providing crisis intervention, resource navigation, and follow-up support to individuals and families affected by substance use disorders. I also collaborated with healthcare providers, treatment facilities, recovery organizations, and community agencies to improve access to treatment and promote continuity of care. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate with individuals during vulnerable moments, identify their needs, explain available resources, and help them determine appropriate next steps with empathy and professionalism.

Previously, as a Social Family Service Worker with the Morris County Department of Human Services, Office of Temporary Assistance, I conducted wellness and needs assessments through both in-person and virtual interviews to determine program eligibility and connect clients with appropriate services. This experience provided me with valuable skills in conducting virtual client interactions, gathering and evaluating information, explaining available resources, and documenting client needs and outcomes. Combined with my experience managing active caseloads of more than 100 clients, I understand the importance of accurate documentation, consistent follow-up, and organized case management to ensure individuals receive timely support.

My experience as a Social Case Worker with the Morris County Sheriff's Office further strengthened my ability to coordinate services for individuals experiencing substance use challenges, mental health concerns, housing instability, and other complex needs. I worked closely with service providers and state agencies, tracked client progress, and maintained accurate records to support effective service delivery. Across these roles, I have developed the ability to manage competing priorities independently, maintain professional communication, and build collaborative relationships with clients, families, and community partners.

In addition, my bachelor's degree in Art Therapy, Crisis Intervention Training, Adult Mental Health First Aid certification, and QPR Suicide Prevention Gatekeeper Training have provided me with a valuable foundation for understanding mental health needs and responding to individuals experiencing difficult circumstances. I am proficient in Microsoft Office, records management systems, data tracking, and virtual communication platforms, and I am comfortable learning new technologies and procedures to support efficient, confidential, and organized operations.

What particularly appeals to me about this opportunity is the chance to make a meaningful difference at the very beginning of someone's treatment journey. I recognize that reaching out for help can be difficult for individuals and families, and I believe that a compassionate, supportive first interaction can help build trust and encourage individuals to pursue care. I would welcome the opportunity to use my experience in virtual assessments, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and client engagement to help prospective clients navigate the admissions process and connect with appropriate treatment services.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience in social services, virtual client assessments, substance use recovery support, and case management could contribute to the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I look forward to the possibility of joining your team and helping individuals and families take meaningful steps toward healing.

Sincerely,
Casey Miller

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. As a student at Southern Utah University pursuing my bachelor’s degree in Family Life and Human Development with a concentration in Family Studies, I have developed a strong interest in helping individuals and families navigate difficult situations and find the support they need. I am passionate about making a positive difference in people’s lives, and I would love the opportunity to be part of a team that helps people take the first step toward healing.

Through my education and experience working with children and families, I have learned the importance of patience, compassion, communication, and understanding. I have worked as a nanny and babysitter, cared for children of different ages, and gained experience working in a girls’ home. These experiences have taught me how important it is to make people feel safe, respected, and supported, especially when they are going through challenging circumstances. I would bring that same caring and nonjudgmental approach to every interaction with clients and families reaching out for help.

I am an organized, dependable, and hardworking person who takes responsibility seriously. I understand the importance of following through, communicating clearly, keeping information organized, and treating personal information with confidentiality. My education has also strengthened my understanding of family relationships, human development, and the challenges individuals and families can face. I am eager to continue learning and developing the skills needed to help connect people with appropriate resources and care.

What interests me most about this opportunity is the chance to make a difference from the very first conversation. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be difficult, and I would strive to make every caller feel heard, respected, and encouraged about their next steps. I would be proud to contribute to an organization that helps individuals and families find hope and access the support they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and passion for helping others could contribute to your team. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,
Lyndee Gale

Dear Sir or Madam, 

Thank you for the opportunity to apply for a position at your company. After reviewing your job description, you are looking for a candidate who is very familiar with the responsibilities associated with the role and can perform them confidently. Given these requirements, I am certain that I have the necessary skills to do the job successfully and meet your expectations. I believe that your company is perfect for my future career.

I completed my Bachelor of Science degree in Psychology Pre-Counseling on December 13, 2024, maintaining a GPA of 3.833 at Capella University. In my professional career, I have many years of experience in Banking, Customer Service, Logistics, Assessments, Triage, and Crisis. I have had the privilege of working for Pyramid Healthcare Inc. as a Needs Assessment Coordinator. I gained valuable professional skills such as assessments, triage, crisis management, medical insurance, managing charts, scheduling, and performing clerical duties. In my academic and professional life, I have been consistently praised while obtaining Honors in The National Society of Leadership and Success, Golden Key International Honor Society, The National Society of Collegiate Scholars, and PSI CHI International Honor Society in Psychology. While working on academic and professional projects, I apply proven communication, management, and leadership skills, which I hope to leverage in the role at your company.

After reviewing my resume, I hope you agree that I am the competent and competitive candidate you seek. I look forward to discussing how my specific skills and abilities will benefit your organization. During our meeting, I will be happy to explain any concerns you may have with breaks in employment. 

I appreciate your consideration and look forward to hearing from you soon. 

Sincerely, 

Stacie Wilson

In my current position as a Behavioral Health Technician at West Valley Medical Center, I maintain detailed and timely documentation, communicate with patients and medical professionals, follow established policies and procedures, and manage responsibilities independently in a fast-paced environment. This experience has strengthened my ability to remain organized, professional, and composed while handling sensitive information and situations requiring sound judgment.
 
My previous experience as a Certified Pharmacy Technician and Certified Medical Assistant provided extensive administrative experience that directly relates to this position. I performed detailed data entry, maintained records, processed billing and insurance information, coordinated appointments, prepared documentation, communicated with customers and professionals, and carefully reviewed information for accuracy. I also have experience handling cash transactions and working with confidential information while consistently following regulatory and organizational requirements.
